speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the cause, how would you describe the onset of these symptoms and is the pain localized to a specific spot or more diffuse?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis) with secondary cellulitis.

The combination of recent Minnesota camping, a self-resolving monoarthritis (knee), and now acute monoarthritis (wrist) with fever and skin lesions is classic for Lyme disease. I am requesting a Two-tier serologic test for Borrelia burgdorferi and a wrist X-Ray to rule out septic arthritis.
